query: Consider the following context: High entropy alloys have excellent wear resistance, so they have great application prospects in the fields of wear resistance and surface protection. In that context, which material can be used for adhere to the surface of a Cu matrix, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Depositing a CoCrFeMnNi high entropy alloy (HEA) coating onto a copper matrix will improve surface wear resistance and adhesion by forming a graded interfacial layer where interdiffusion creates a metallurgical bond that reduces stress concentrations.
generation.material_initial_state: A copper matrix with its typical native oxide layer and microstructure.
generation.intervention: Application of a CoCrFeMnNi high entropy alloy layer onto the copper substrate using a thermal spray deposition process.
generation.conditions: Room temperature or moderate temperature deposition with controlled cooling to minimize thermal mismatch; subsequent wear testing under standard conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: A graded interfacial zone where interdiffused copper and HEA elements form a metallurgical bond that mechanically interlocks the coating with the substrate.
generation.mechanism: The HEA provides high hardness and excellent wear resistance, while moderate interdiffusion at the interface produces a transition zone that chemically and mechanically bonds the coating to the Cu matrix. This reduces residual stresses and enhances load transfer during wear.
generation.predicted_outcome: The coated sample is expected to exhibit an improved wear resistance and stronger adhesion compared to an uncoated Cu substrate, as demonstrated by lower wear rates and higher adhesion strength in standardized tests.
generation.baseline: Wearing performance and adhesion metrics measured on untreated or conventionally coated Cu substrates.
generation.boundary: The improvement in adhesion and wear resistance may be limited if the deposition conditions lead to either insufficient interdiffusion or an overly thick interfacial layer, which could adversely affect ductility or induce thermal stresses under extreme cyclic load or temperature variations.
generation.uncertainty: The exact thickness and composition of the graded interfacial layer, as well as its long-term stability under cyclic mechanical and thermal stresses, are not fully quantified.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of copper substrates with a thermal-sprayed CoCrFeMnNi HEA coating and one set with no coating (or a conventional coating). Subject both sets to identical wear tests (e.g., pin-on-disk) and adhesion tests (e.g., scratch tests) while performing microstructural analysis at the interface using SEM/EDS.
measurements: Wear rate (mass loss or volume loss)
Coefficient of friction during wear test
Adhesion strength measured by critical load in a scratch test
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the HEA-coated Cu substrates do not demonstrate statistically significant improvements in both wear resistance and adhesion strength (e.g., similar wear rates and critical loads in scratch tests) compared to the baseline, or if no graded interfacial layer is observed, then the hypothesis will be considered falsified.
